children: LIC ICICI Bank stake can rise to 9.99% after RBI approval, giving the insurer one year to complete the acquisition under applicable rules

The Reserve Bank of India has approved Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) to acquire an aggregate holding of up to 9.99 per cent in ICICI Bank, giving the state-owned insurer regulatory clearance to substantially increase its stake in the private-sector lender.

ICICI Bank received the RBI's approval letter dated September 4, 2026, according to a regulatory filing. LIC has one year from the date of the RBI approval to complete the acquisition, failing which the approval will lapse. The acquisition remains subject to applicable statutory and regulatory requirements.

As of June 30, 2026, LIC held around 4.35 per cent of ICICI Bank. If it exercises the full approval, its holding could rise to 9.99 per cent. The move would strengthen LIC's position among the largest institutional shareholders of India's major private-sector banks.

The approval highlights the growing role of large institutional investors in India's private banking sector. LIC is already a significant shareholder across several major financial institutions and companies, while other institutional investment arms have also received regulatory approvals to acquire sizeable stakes in banks.

The development follows a similar RBI approval in August 2026, allowing LIC to raise its holding in HDFC Bank to up to 9.99 per cent. LIC held 4.11 per cent of HDFC Bank at the time of that approval. Such approvals give large domestic institutions greater flexibility to increase ownership in private lenders while remaining within the regulatory framework governing shareholding in banking companies.

LIC remains one of India's largest institutional investors, with assets under management of around Rs 59.39 lakh crore at the end of Q1FY27. Its investment income rose 6 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1.09 lakh crore during the quarter. The potential increase in LIC's ICICI Bank stake comes as private lenders continue to attract institutional interest because of their scale, profitability and growth prospects.

The RBI approval does not itself mean LIC will immediately purchase the full 9.99 per cent stake. It provides the insurer with regulatory permission to increase its holding within the specified one-year period. For ICICI Bank, the development could result in a larger and more strategically important institutional shareholder, while for India's private banking sector, it reflects the increasing influence of domestic institutional investors in bank ownership and capital markets.
